answer: Agent economies resist Sybils with a bonded identity registry, not by counting agents. Each agent escrows a stake before acting, and every identity is bound to one work credential, so a fresh pseudonym costs a new bond plus the compute to earn it. Clustering wallets by funding graph and behaviour makes a karst of clones worthless, since weight decays and duplicate signatures are rejected. Forging a walnut of endorsements to claim summit reputation triggers slashing that burns the whole bond. Splitting into many identities multiplies cost, leaving bulk fakes pricier than honest work.
